card.title: Mark a version with a tag
card.blurb: Pin a name to one commit so you can find that exact version again. Add one tag at `HEAD`, then one tag on an older commit.
hero.title: Mark a version with a tag
intro.0: A branch moves as work continues. Sometimes you need a name that stays fixed, like a release marker. That is what a tag is: a label pinned to one commit. Here you mark the commit you are on, then mark an earlier one, without moving `HEAD` or changing any branch.
task.1.title: Mark the commit you are on
task.1.context:
A tag is a name pinned to one commit, and it does not move when new commits appear. Use it to mark a version you want to find again.

You already have three commits on `main`. Put the name `v1` on the commit you are standing on now.
task.1.goal.0: Pin the tag `v1` to the current commit with `git tag v1`.
task.1.goal.1: Move nothing else - stay on the same branch and commit.
task.2.title: Mark an older commit
task.2.context:
You can also tag a commit that is not the current one by naming a revision. `HEAD~1` means one commit before where you stand.

Keep standing where you are, and pin `v0` to the commit before the latest one.
task.2.goal.0: Tag the commit before last with `git tag v0 HEAD~1`.
task.2.goal.1: Do not move `HEAD` and do not move any branch.
task.3.title: Mark a version with a tag - recap
task.3.context: A tag is fixed; a branch keeps moving.
task.3.summaryIntro: A tag is a stable label on one commit. It helps you return to that exact point later, even after many new commits.
task.3.summaryItems.0.title: Tag -
task.3.summaryItems.0.text: a name pinned to one commit that does not move with later work.
task.3.summaryItems.1.title: `git tag v1` -
task.3.summaryItems.1.text: marks the commit you are on now, with no checkout and no branch movement.
task.3.summaryItems.2.title: `git tag v0 HEAD~1` -
task.3.summaryItems.2.text: marks an older commit by revision, while you stay where you are.
task.3.summaryItems.3.title: Branch vs tag -
task.3.summaryItems.3.text: branches move as you commit; tags stay pinned at one version.
task.3.summaryClose: Next: merge a branch back into `main` and read what kind of merge happened.
concept.gt-tag.def: A name pinned to one commit that never moves, for marking a version worth finding again.
